business_problem: Pacers Sports & Entertainment needed a custom captioning system that could keep up with fast, unscripted basketball commentary and deliver accurate live captions and translations to deaf, hard-of-hearing, and non-English-speaking fans on arena displays and in its mobile apps.
solution_summary: Pacers Sports & Entertainment built a real-time captioning stack on Microsoft Azure to turn live game commentary into synchronized captions across Gainbridge Fieldhouse screens and the Pacers and Fever mobile apps. Azure AI Foundry provided a secure, containerized environment for training and refining custom Azure AI Speech models with hundreds of hours of Pacers and Fever broadcasts plus structured lists of player, coach, and official names. In production, announcer audio is transcribed and translated by Azure AI Speech, then Azure Functions processes caption events and Azure SignalR Service pushes them to a single endpoint used by both in-arena displays and the mobile app with virtually no lag. The architecture gave PS&E near-instant English captions, added Spanish, and created a path to roll out 12 additional languages and more AI-powered fan experiences.

solution_components.name: Azure AI Foundry
solution_components.role: Provides the secure environment where PS&E trains, tests, and refines custom speech models before release.

solution_components.name: Azure AI Speech
solution_components.role: Transcribes and translates live announcer audio using models tuned to basketball terminology, names, and cadence.

solution_components.name: Azure Functions
solution_components.role: Processes caption events and coordinates real-time delivery from the speech service to client endpoints.

solution_components.name: Azure SignalR Service
solution_components.role: Streams synchronized captions to arena displays and mobile clients with virtually no perceptible delay.

data_flow: Live announcer audio is sent into Azure AI Speech models trained in Azure AI Foundry, where it is transcribed and translated in real time. Azure Functions processes the caption output and Azure SignalR Service publishes it to a shared endpoint that keeps the Pacers and Fever mobile apps and Gainbridge Fieldhouse displays in sync.
business_outcome: PS&E launched the first live in-arena and mobile captioning experience of its kind for Pacers and Fever games, reduced caption error to 1.14%, cut model-training preparation time from days to minutes, and created a scalable foundation for multilingual and future AI-powered fan experiences.
metrics: Caption error rate reduced to just 1.14%
Speech-to-text transcription error rate reduced by 87%
Audio preparation for a single game reduced from upwards of five days to roughly two minutes
12 additional languages planned after the initial English and Spanish rollout
architecture_clues: The custom training dataset used hundreds of hours of Pacers and Fever broadcasts.
Structured text files with player, coach, and official names improved domain-specific transcription accuracy.
Captions are delivered through a single event-driven endpoint shared by mobile and in-arena displays.
Built-in moderation filters prevent inappropriate or misinterpreted content from reaching the screen.
PS&E used a standard WebView to keep client integration simple for future expansion.
